top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Strade Bianche's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Strade Bianche. Practice on compacted earth/clay with crushed stones—the: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 86 miles.
76ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
6,560ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 86, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Gran Fondo Strade Bianche, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Strade Bianche. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Strade Bianche. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on compacted earth/clay with crushed stones—the can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
6,560ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,560ft of climbing on compacted earth/clay with crushed stones—the does to your power file on race day.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 86 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.weather: March in Siena, Tuscany, Italy — March in Tuscany is a gamble. Best case: cool spring sun (10-15°C), dusty and fast. Worst case: 'epic' cold rain (2-8°C) where white dust turns to grey paste that destroys brake pads and drivetrains. Mornings near freezing—arm warmers and gilets mandatory at start. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Gran Fondo Strade Bianche. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Strade Bianche’s 86 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Strade Bianche rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on compacted earth/clay with crushed stones—the famous 'strade bianche' to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 86 miles of compacted earth/clay with crushed stones—the famous 'strade bianche' in Siena, Tuscany, Italy.
